# opstracer_mute (Resource)

Silences every alert of a service or an integration for a time window, like a maintenance window. To silence only some alerts of a service, use `opstracer_suppression`. A mute cannot be edited, so any change replaces it, except writing the same time in another UTC offset. Once the window is over the mute stays in state as inactive; a mute ended early outside Terraform is created again. Destroy ends a running mute and removes a scheduled one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Silence every alert of the checkout service during a maintenance window.
resource "opstracer_mute" "checkout_maintenance" {
  scope_type = "service"
  scope_id   = opstracer_service.checkout.id
  starts_at  = "2026-11-01T22:00:00+07:00"
  ends_at    = "2026-11-02T01:00:00+07:00"
  reason     = "Database upgrade"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ends_at` (String) RFC 3339 end of the window. Must be in the future and after `starts_at`.
- `scope_id` (String) ID of the service or integration to mute.
- `scope_type` (String) What to mute: `service` or `integration`.

### Optional

- `reason` (String) Why alerts are muted.
- `starts_at` (String) RFC 3339 start of the window, e.g. `2026-10-20T09:00:00+07:00`. Defaults to the time of creation.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the mute is silencing alerts right now. False before the start and after the end.
- `id` (String) Mute ID.
- `service_id` (String) Service the mute applies to.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Only scheduled and running mutes can be imported.
terraform import opstracer_mute.checkout_maintenance <mute-id>
```
